text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: hosted-api p99 > 12s, queue growing in us-west-2. Auto-escalation to SRE.

emily_sre: seeing a sharp spike in requests since 18:02 UTC, p95 jumped from 220ms -> 3.1s in 3m. p99 ~ 12.4s. Queue length at ingress: 48,200 requests, dropping ~ no tokens from GPU pool.

raj_oncall: on it. Can someone confirm if autoscaler created GPUs?

alex_infra: provisioner logs show repeated failures around 18:03: "CreateInstance failed: quotaExceeded: GPU quota in us-west-2". Also a handful of 429s from cloud-api (rateLimitExceeded).

olivia_prodeng: this originated from a marketing campaign burst - customer_campaign_id=mk-2234. Seen a 4200x burst from a single API key across many clients.

maria_cs: notifying customer CSM now, flags: possible degraded experience. Jen, can you draft a status update if we see >10% errors?

jen_support: on it. Draft ready, will hold until we confirm mitigation.

emily_sre: mitigation options: 1) enable emergency rate-limit on that API key (recommended), 2) route low-cost fallback model (smaller) for non-critical requests, 3) drain queue to degenerate endpoints.

raj_oncall: apply rate limit now and enable fallback routing to gpt-small-quantized. Who can change routing?

olivia_prodeng: I can flip routing policy to prefer gpt-small for that key. Doing: \n```\n# switch route\nredwoodctl routing set --key mk-2234 --prefer-model gpt-small-quant --timeout-ms 5000\n```\n
incidents-bot: Executed routing update (olivia_prodeng) at 18:12 UTC.

alex_infra: autoscaler still failing to create new GPU nodes because quota + API rate limit. We tried a soft-queue fallback that spins up CPU-backed workers but those are at capacity too.

emily_sre: Starting active queue-shedding for that key: DROP new streaming requests > 2r/s, allow a slow-lane with reduced tokens. Applying now.

incidents-bot: Rate-limit applied to key mk-2234 by emily_sre (2r/s).

raj_oncall: quick check: what did p95/p99 move to after routing + rate-limit?

emily_sre: p95 now 430ms, p99 2.1s for overall traffic. For the affected key we see much improved tail but still some backlog. Queue length dropped from 48,200 -> 9,600 in 6m.

olivia_prodeng: fallback to gpt-small reduced per-request GPU time from ~350ms/token to ~90ms/token. Good win on throughput.

alex_infra: cloud quota request submitted to provider and support ticket opened (ticket# CLOUD-9817). But approvals won't be immediate.

maria_cs: customer notified: "We’ve applied temporary rate-limits and routing to reduce impact. Investigating root cause; will update in 30m."

jen_support: posting to status page draft now.

emily_sre: still seeing intermittent 504s for long-lived streaming sessions stuck in backend queue. Mitigation: enable aggressive per-connection timeouts and abort long KV-cache warmups.

olivia_prodeng: enabled streaming abort threshold to 6s for warmup requests. Also toggled prefix-caching TTL to 30s to reduce KV pressure.

incidents-bot: Metric alert suppressed by emily_sre at 18:21 UTC (manual).

raj_oncall: handoff plan: I'll stay until backlog < 1k and p99 < 500ms, or until 20:00 UTC. If not met, escalate to infra lead.

alex_infra: note: provisioner leader election lagged earlier causing duplicate create attempts and some resources leaked in PENDING. Running cleanup: \n```\n# remove stuck instances\ncloudctl instances list --filter status=PENDING | xargs cloudctl instances delete\n```\n
emily_sre: recording timeline for postmortem:
- 18:02 UTC: marketing-driven burst begins
- 18:03 UTC: autoscaler attempts to create GPUs -> quotaExceeded
- 18:06 UTC: queue > 30k, p99 > 10s
- 18:12 UTC: routing switch to gpt-small, rate-limits applied
- 18:18 UTC: queue reduced to ~9.6k, p99 ~2.1s
- 18:30 UTC: aiming for service stable metrics

olivia_prodeng: temporary mitigations summary: rate-limit mk-2234 (2r/s), route mk-2234 -> gpt-small-quant, reduce streaming warmup timeout to 6s, ttl down for prefix-cache.

maria_cs: customer escalations: one enterprise client reported 15% error rate. CS team will prioritize refunds/credits if SLA breached.

jen_support: status page published: "Degraded performance for hosted-api in us-west-2 due to traffic spike. Temporary mitigations applied. Investigating." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/6162012345

raj_oncall: handoff note for night team: if queue > 3k or p99 > 1s re-open paging and engage infra lead @alex_infra. Also keep rate-limits in place until autoscaler can reliably provision GPUs.

incidents-bot: PagerDuty note: Incident acked by raj_oncall at 18:25 UTC.

emily_sre: follow-ups for postmortem: check autoscaler retry/backoff, cloud quota pre-warm plan, per-customer burst protection rules, and leader election robustness.

olivia_prodeng: adding model fallback as automated policy: if pool utilization >85% for 30s, auto-route non-critical keys to smaller models.

alex_infra: I'll request emergency quota bump and follow up on CLOUD-9817. Also adding guardrails to avoid duplicate create attempts during leader flaps.

maria_cs: closing loop with customer in 45m unless more impact reported.

jen_support: notes added to ticketing system and support playbook updated with this mitigation set.

raj_oncall: I'm leaving an oncall note: "Mitigations applied; primary risk = cloud GPU quota and provisioner rate-limit. If quota not granted and traffic persists, additional rate-limits and broader fallback to CPU-workers will be needed."

incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigated (degraded) at 18:40 UTC. Keep thread for postmortem inputs.

emily_sre: thanks team. I'll own the postmortem draft and link this thread.

olivia_prodeng: +1 — will add perf numbers and model delta analysis.

maria_cs: will follow up on customer outcomes and compensation if necessary.

pagerduty: Incident resolved acknowledgement sent to on-call.

(End of thread)
